title: Power Apps: model-driven apps as Business Applications in Work IQ
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap record and Microsoft documentation, including the control paths and both Dataverse calls. It correctly distinguishes the default-on exclusions, deferred enablement of existing environments, experience-based billing and conflicting release descriptions.

claims.claim: Work IQ is on by default for qualifying new public production environments.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments created for new or existing tenants. The following environments are exceptions:

claims.claim: EU and EFTA environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: **European Union (EU) and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) environments**: This exception applies to environments provisioned in the EU and EFTA macro region geography.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Government-related environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: **Government-related environments**: This exception applies to environments provisioned by customers with current or previous government cloud deployments that are likely to depend on FedRAMP security controls.

claims.claim: Trial, sandbox and developer environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: **Nonproduction environments**: This exception applies to trial, sandbox, and developer environments.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Work IQ respects existing Power Platform permissions when selecting environments and apps and accessing data.
claims.quote: Work IQ respects your existing Power Platform security permissions. You can only select environments and applications, view data, and perform actions that your permissions allow.

claims.claim: Work IQ does not grant additional access to business data.
claims.quote: If the app appears but data is missing, confirm your Dataverse security roles and record access. Work IQ doesn't grant additional access to business data.

claims.claim: Enabling Work IQ might send data from a FedRAMP-accredited environment to Microsoft 365 outside its applicable boundary.
claims.quote: Enabling Work IQ might cause data to flow from the tenant's FedRAMP-accredited environment to Microsoft 365, which is outside the applicable FedRAMP authorization boundary.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Consumption billing applies to the Work IQ API and Copilot Studio entry points, with treatment following the experience.
claims.quote: Copilot credits are the unit used for the participating usage-based experiences. Prepaid capacity packs and pay-as-you-go billing through an Azure subscription provide ways to fund that consumption.

claims.claim: Costs are tracked by consuming experience rather than a dedicated Business Applications category.
claims.quote: For Business Applications in Work IQ, you track cost by the experiences people use rather than by a dedicated business applications category.

claims.claim: Work IQ in Copilot Studio is powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness.
claims.quote: Work IQ in Copilot Studio is powered by the [Microsoft Copilot harness](../harnesses-overview), which uses Copilot Credits for [usage-based billing](billing-credit-overview).

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ in Copilot Studio uses Copilot Credits for usage-based billing.
claims.quote: Work IQ uses the Microsoft Copilot harness and Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: A separate spending policy is not required for Work IQ in Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Work IQ uses consumption billing. A separate spending policy isn't required for Work IQ.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ consumption supporting a Cowork task is attributed to Cowork.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Direct Work IQ calls from coding agents or custom integrations are reported under Work IQ API.
claims.quote: **Coding agents or custom integrations that call Work IQ directly**: Consumption through that connection appears under Work IQ API.

claims.claim: Work IQ API consumption can combine Microsoft 365 and business applications context.
claims.quote: Work IQ API consumption can include both Microsoft 365 productivity context and business applications context. Its total is not a Business Applications-only cost breakdown.

claims.claim: The applicable Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat entitlement includes business-data grounding in the licensed chat scenario.
claims.quote: **Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat**: The applicable entitlement includes business-data grounding in the licensed chat scenario. You don't pay extra for it as a Work IQ API interaction.

claims.claim: One request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps.
claims.quote: One user request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Cost per prompt varies with the consuming experience and work performed.
claims.quote: Work IQ includes deterministic operations and variable-cost contextual reasoning, so a prompt isn't necessarily a single fixed-price operation. Complexity, the context needed, and the work performed affect consumption.

claims.claim: PATCH <organization-url>/api/data/v9.2/applications(<application-id>) can set access to 1 (Blocked) or 0 (Allowed).

Entity set path:
- [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/applications
Primary key:
- applicationid
Operations supported:
- POSTGETPATCHDELETE
access | Edm.Int32 | Application Access
0 | Allowed
1 | Blocked

claims.claim: The app setting is at Power Apps > Apps > app > Edit > Settings > Features > Enable Microsoft 365 Copilot in model-driven apps.
claims.quote:
Select **Apps**.
